subject: POC prompt/eval dataset collection  next steps and files needed
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Gupta <priya.gupta@stellaretail.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: POC prompt/eval dataset collection - follow-up and success criteria

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time to walk through StellarRetail's use cases today - really helpful context. As discussed, we want to make the POC as focused and measurable as possible. Below is a short recap and the ask for the prompt/log dataset you mentioned. Can you confirm ownership and timeline for these items?

POC scope (recap)
- Primary objective: Validate Redwood inference improves cashier-assist response accuracy and reduces average rework by >= 20% on returns-handling scenarios.
- Target surface: in-store POS suggestions + suggested return reason classification.
- Success criteria: accuracy uplift vs baseline on curated prompt set, latency <= 350ms p50, and cost per 1k tokens within projected threshold.

Dataset request (what we need from StellarRetail)
1) Prompt set: ~300 representative prompts (customer queries / returns scenarios). Prefer CSV with columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_label/expected_response (where known), metadata (store_id optional).
2) Model/eval logs: 2 weeks of anonymized POS query logs (sample of 5k lines) - strip PII; a readme describing redaction steps.
3) Priority cases: call out 30 "high-impact" prompts where errors are business-critical.

Timelines & ownership
- Priya/Anita: provide sample prompt CSV and one-week of logs by Fri 9 Apr (we can accept a staged delivery).
- Redwood (Marissa/Connor): ingest dataset, define evaluation plan, and deliver initial eval & recommendation by Fri 16 Apr.

Format/requirements notes
- CSV preferred (UTF-8). If logs are JSONL, please include a sample schema.
- Provide any scoring guidance you have (e.g., business labels, pass/fail rules).

Next steps
- Priya: share two example prompt rows and the readme so Connor can validate ingestion format.
- Marissa: will share a short eval plan doc + Drive folder for uploads once we have the sample.

Appreciate it - if the timeline looks tight, we can shift to a 1-week buffer.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood_poc_eval_plan_template.docx]

From: Priya Gupta <priya.gupta@stellaretail.com>

Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC prompt/eval dataset collection - follow-up and success criteria

Thanks Marissa - this is great and aligns with what we discussed. I'm confirming Anita and I will own the prompt/log collection. A few quick notes:

- We can deliver an initial sample of ~300 prompts, and we have internal labels for ~40% of them.
- Logs: we can provide anonymized logs as JSONL; we'll include a readme describing fields and the redaction script we use.
- Priority list: we'll flag 35 high-impact prompts.

I'll upload a zipped sample (3 sample prompts + logs readme) to the Drive link you provide, or I can attach to email if that's easier. Targeting Fri 9 Apr delivery.

One question for Connor: our logs include session_id, user_message, store_id, and a timestamp. We currently redact user identifiers; is session_id OK to keep for dedup/aggregation?

- Priya
Senior Product Manager, StellarRetail

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Gupta <priya.gupta@stellaretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC prompt/eval dataset collection - follow-up and success criteria

Hi Priya - thanks for the quick reply and for owning the dataset. Session_id is fine to keep as long as it is a non-PII hashed token (not reversible to a real user id). That helps a lot for deduping and session-level evaluation. A couple of technical preferences from our side:

- Prompt CSV: include a prompt_id (string), prompt_text (UTF-8), expected_label/expected_response (optional), and source_tag (e.g., "agent", "web", "in-store").
- Logs: JSONL is perfect. Please include a small sample (10-20 lines) in the initial delivery so we can validate the pipeline.
- Redaction readme: include the exact fields removed or hashed and the hashing algorithm (e.g., SHA-256 with salt).

I'll prepare a short ingestion checklist and post it to the Drive once Marissa creates the folder. If you want, we can do a 20-minute call Thurs to align on schema.

Connor
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
